nodes.text: Mind the dust. That's good *flour*, not dirt. Garton. Forty years at this wheel, boy and man. The pond hasn't missed a day's work yet. More than I can say for anyone else in this town.

choices.text: What's your quarrel with the ferry bell?
Forty years. The town must have changed.

nodes.text: Quarrel! It's not a quarrel, it's a *position*. That bell rings on a west wind whether there's a soul at the crossing or not, and it scares my herons off the shallows. I've raised it at the moot. Twice. Mind you, the boy checks my mooring lines every morning like it's nothing. So the bell stays. Don't you go fixing it.

Changed? When I started, the Round was mud, the bank was a toll box, and Silverfall silver came through four caravans a season. Then the mountain sealed its cellar, the caravans thinned, and this town learnt to feed itself: fields, pond, orchard. Now the cellar's open again and everyone's dreaming of silver. *Flour*, I tell them. You can't eat silver. Nobody listens.
Flour by the sack, wheat by the sheaf, and a loaf if the morning batch behaved.
Passing's free. Gossip's free too, and mine's more reliable than what you'll hear at Dunna's inn.
